paragraphs.title: The Prophet's Mission and the Light to the Nations

answers: From the beginning of his reign
easy.explanation: The Lord says, “The Lord hath called me from the womb.”
easy.q: When was the servant called by the Lord?

easy.explanation: The verse says, “He hath made my mouth like a sharp sword.”
easy.q: What was the servant's mouth made like?

easy.explanation: The servant was given “for a light to the Gentiles.”
easy.q: To whom was the servant given as a light?

answers: He hid him in the shadow of His hand
He sent him immediately to every nation
He left him without a mission
medium.explanation: The Lord says, “In the shadow of his hand hath he hid me.”
medium.q: What did the Lord do with the servant until the proper time?

answers: He felt successful and stopped working
He felt he had laboured in vain, but left his judgment with the Lord
He became angry and abandoned his mission
medium.explanation: He said he had laboured “in vain,” yet his judgment and work were with the Lord.
medium.q: How did the servant feel about his labor, and what conclusion did he reach?

medium.explanation: The mission includes raising up Jacob’s tribes and restoring Israel.
medium.q: What does “to raise up the tribes of Jacob” mean in this passage?

answers: It is limited to one people
It concerns only rebuilding the land
challenge.explanation: The mission expands from restoring Israel to bringing salvation “unto the end of the earth.”
challenge.q: What does the movement from restoring Israel to being a light to the Gentiles show about the mission?

answers: His speech is a chief tool of his mission
His speech is meant only to conceal him
His speech keeps him from acting
challenge.explanation: The sharp sword pictures the power and effectiveness of the servant’s words.
challenge.q: What is the connection between the sharp mouth and the servant's mission?

answers: He becomes hidden from the nations
Kings and princes will honor him
challenge.explanation: Kings shall see and arise, and princes shall worship him.
challenge.q: What change comes to the one who was despised and rejected?

paragraphs.title: The Promise of Redemption and the Road for the Returning

easy.explanation: The Lord says, “I have heard thee,” “I have helped thee,” and “I will preserve thee.”
easy.q: What does the Lord promise to do in the acceptable time and day of salvation?

easy.explanation: The servant was to say to the prisoners, “Go forth.”
easy.q: What were the prisoners told to do?

easy.explanation: The verse says, “They shall not hunger nor thirst.”
easy.q: What would the returning people not suffer from?

answers: To establish the land and give desolate inheritances to be possessed
medium.explanation: The covenant would establish the earth and give people the desolate heritages.
medium.q: Why was the servant given as a covenant of the people?

answers: The mountains would be removed entirely
The mountains would become a way and the highways would be raised
medium.explanation: The Lord says, “I will make all my mountains a way, and my highways shall be exalted.”
medium.q: How would the way be prepared for the returning people?

answers: Places where the returning people could feed
medium.explanation: The returning people would feed along the ways and find pastures in high places.
medium.q: In this passage, what does “pastures ... in all high places” describe?

answers: He leads them to springs of water and places of pasture
They no longer need food or water
challenge.explanation: The Lord leads them and guides them by the springs of water.
challenge.q: What is the connection between the Lord's guidance and the people's lack of hunger and thirst?

answers: From far away, from the north, the west, and the land of Sinim
challenge.explanation: The passage names people coming from far, from the north, the west, and the land of Sinim.
challenge.q: From which directions are the returning people described as coming?

answers: The Lord has comforted His people and had mercy on the afflicted
challenge.explanation: Their rejoicing is based on the Lord’s comfort and mercy toward His people.
challenge.q: Why are the heavens, earth, and mountains called to rejoice?

paragraphs.title: Zion's Comfort and the Return of Her Children

answers: The Lord has forsaken and forgotten her
easy.explanation: Zion says, “The Lord hath forsaken me, and my Lord hath forgotten me.”
easy.q: What does Zion say about herself?

answers: Upon the palms of His hands
On the top of a mountain
easy.explanation: The Lord says, “I have graven thee upon the palms of my hands.”
easy.q: Where did the Lord say He had engraved Zion?

answers: They will gather and come to her
easy.explanation: Zion is told to behold her children gathering and coming to her.
easy.q: What will happen to Zion's children?

medium.explanation: The Lord asks whether a woman can forget her sucking child, and says He will not forget Zion.
medium.q: What relationship does the Lord use to describe His bond with Zion?

answers: They will leave and go away from her
medium.explanation: The verse says, “Thy destroyers ... shall go forth of thee.”
medium.q: What will happen to Zion's destroyers?

answers: There is not enough room because many children have come
The city has been completely destroyed
The city is far from the land
medium.explanation: The place becomes too narrow because of the multitude of inhabitants.
medium.q: What does the statement “The place is too strait for me” mean?

answers: A desolate city becomes a city filled with children
A rich city becomes merely poor
A city among mountains loses its roads
challenge.explanation: Zion is first described as desolate and forsaken, then as filled with returning children.
challenge.q: What major contrast appears in the description of Zion?

answers: The Lord is always mindful of Zion's condition
The walls have disappeared from the land
Zion does not need her children
challenge.explanation: The walls being continually before the Lord emphasizes His constant remembrance of Zion.
challenge.q: What can be understood from the words, “Thy walls are continually before me”?

answers: She thought she was alone, captive, and bereaved
The children had never belonged to her
The city did not know the Lord
challenge.explanation: Zion had believed she was left alone, so the appearance of many children astonishes her.
challenge.q: Why is Zion surprised by the children who return?

paragraphs.title: The Return of the Children and Victory over the Adversaries

easy.explanation: The Lord says that the Gentiles shall bring Zion’s sons and daughters.

answers: They will serve as nursing fathers and mothers
easy.explanation: Kings will be her nursing fathers, and queens her nursing mothers.
easy.q: What will kings and queens do for Zion?

easy.explanation: The Lord says, “I will save thy children.”
easy.q: What does the Lord promise to do for Zion's children?

answers: That they are sent far away
medium.explanation: The images of arms and shoulders portray the children being brought home safely and carefully.
medium.q: What does carrying the children in arms and upon shoulders suggest?

answers: Can a captive be delivered from one stronger than himself?
Is there enough room in the city?
medium.explanation: The passage asks whether the prey can be taken from the mighty and the lawful captive delivered.
medium.q: What question is raised by the picture of a captive held by a mighty man?

answers: Captives or spoil taken by an enemy
medium.explanation: The following verse speaks of captives and prey being delivered from the mighty.
medium.q: What does “the prey” refer to in this context?

answers: He promises to take the mighty man's captives and save them
He agrees that rescue is impossible
He tells the captives to save themselves
challenge.explanation: The Lord promises that even the captives of the mighty shall be taken away and delivered.
challenge.q: How does the Lord answer the claim that a captive cannot be rescued from a mighty enemy?

answers: The nations bring the children, the Lord opposes their enemies, and He saves them
The children disappear and the kings destroy the city
The queens hide the children and the Gentiles begin a war
challenge.explanation: The nations bring Zion’s children, and the Lord then contends with her adversary and saves them.
challenge.q: What is the main sequence of events in these verses?

answers: All flesh will know that He is Savior and Redeemer
Only the kings of the earth will know Him
challenge.explanation: The chapter ends with all flesh knowing that the Lord is Zion’s Savior and Redeemer.
challenge.q: What will be the final result of the Lord's action?
